```{r}

dir.create(here("Tables", "itol_annotations"), showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

# FILE 1: labels.txt

)

labels

## Morphology

# FILE 2: morphology_colorstrip.txt

# Edit these two colors to change Morphology appearance
morph_colors <- c("Mucoid" = "#4eadb9", "Dry" = "#e0ba3e")
  
morphology <- data.frame(
    tip   = meta_tree$Strain,
    color = morph_colors[as.character(meta_tree$Morphology)],
    label = meta_tree$Morphology
  )

morphology <- morphology[!is.na(morphology$color), ]
morphology

cat(
    "DATASET_COLORSTRIP\n",
    "SEPARATOR TAB\n",
    "DATASET_LABEL\tMorphology\n",

  )

# FILE 3: pairs_colorstrip.txt   (colored boxes + pair numbers)

pair_ids    <- sort(unique(na.omit(as.character(meta_tree$Pairs))))

  tip   = meta_tree$Strain,
  color = pair_colors[as.character(meta_tree$Pairs)],
  label = meta_tree$Pairs
)

cat(
  "DATASET_COLORSTRIP\n",
```

```{r}

raw_lines <- read_lines("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sohini5981/AVT_SS/refs/heads/main/Data/strain_118_variants_pairwise_mismatches.tsv?token=GHSAT0AAAAAAEB5NZNICNZ5L2YG7GHWP4FI2TIXJKA")

# Keep only the actual data rows (they start with "DCv2", not "#DCv2" or "INFO")
data_lines <- raw_lines[startsWith(raw_lines, "DCv2")]
#View(data_lines)
gtcheck_data <- read_tsv(
  I(data_lines),   # I() tells read_tsv to treat this as literal text, not a filepath
  col_names = c("Tag", "Query_Sample", "Genotyped_Sample", "Discordance",
                "Avg_neg_log_P_HWE", "Sites_compared", "Matching_genotypes")
)

#View(gtcheck_data)
gtcheck_data <- gtcheck_data %>% dplyr::select(-Tag)

### Not all of the genotypes that have been compared are paris: 

Pairs <- read_excel(here("Data_input", "Strains_Description_Phenotype_Github.xlsx"))
View(Pairs)
Pairs <- Pairs %>% filter(!is.na(Pairs))

pairs_wide <- Pairs %>%
  select(Strain_Code, Morphology, Pairs) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = Morphology, values_from = Strain_Code)
#View(pairs_wide)

### I am not interested in which is teh query_sample and which one is the genotyped_sample in the strain_118_variants_pairwise_mismatches.tsv

### Sort the two strain names alphabetically first, so the same pair always produces the same key regardless of which strain in gtcheck is query or genotyped

pairs_wide <- pairs_wide %>%
  rowwise() %>% ## rowwise() always goes paired with ungroup(). rowwise() function converts a dataframe. into a special grouped form where every single row is treated as its own individual group
  mutate(pair_key = paste(sort(c(Mucoid, Dry)), collapse = "_")) %>%
  ungroup()


gtcheck_data <- gtcheck_data %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(pair_key = paste(sort(c(Query_Sample, Genotyped_Sample)), collapse = "_")) %>%
  ungroup() ## The idea is to put the two strains names in the same alphabeticl order no matter which one came first. So it will create an identical key of AVT29_AVT98
View(gtcheck_data)


mismatch_filtered <- merge(pairs_wide, gtcheck_data, by = "pair_key")

## I want to calculate the number of SNP differences 

mismatch_filtered <- mismatch_filtered %>%
  mutate(SNP_differences = Sites_compared - Matching_genotypes)


#View(mismatch_filtered)
```

## Incorporate other phenotypic values

I am going to incorporate other phenotypic values to take into account the phylogenetic signal 

```{r}


## I will add them as covariates in my model 
#library(lme4)

model <- lm(ave_shoot ~ Morphology*Variety + PC1 + PC2, data = pheno_merged) ## I am not adding  + (1|Strain_Code) because I am already working with the average of the strains , that is why I use shoot_ave. 
summary(model)
anova(model)

## PC1 is significant. A significant PC1 effect on shoot biomass means that strains that sit further along the dominant genome-wide lineage split tend to have systematically different shoot biomass. That is a real pattern, but it is not attributable to any one gene- PC1 is a composite of thousands of SNPs simultaneously, so there's no signle causal story to tell about "what PC1 does". A way to interprete this is that "broad ancestry/relatedness explains some baseline variation in this trait", similar to controlling for a batch effect. It is rarely something you'd highlight as a biological finding in itself. Without PC1/PC2 in the model, if morphology happens to correlate with deep lineage structure (e.g., mucoid strains cluster more in one part of the phylogeny), I can not tell whether an apparent morphotype -> biomass effect is real, or just relatedness masquerading as a morphotype effect. Including PC1/PC2 "soaks up" the variance explained by broad ancestry first, so the coefficient you get from "Morphology" after is a cleaner estimate of morphotype's effect independent of which lineage a strain happens to belong to. 

model <- lm(Fitness_ave ~ Morphology*Variety + PC1 + PC2, data = pheno_merged) 
summary(model)
anova(model)
model<- lm(Fitness_ave ~ Morphology*Variety, data = pheno_merged)
anova(model)

model <- lm(Fitness_ave ~ Morphology*Variety*ave_shoot, data = pheno_merged)
summary(model)
anova(model)


```

```{r, include= FALSE}

### Pyseer code to run the presence absence data using the binary phenotype where Mucoid is 1 and Dry is 0.

pyseer --lmm --phenotypes Data_input/Binary_phenotype_pyseer.tsv \
  --pres Data_input/gene_presence_absence_rtab_pyseer.tsv \
  --similarity Data_input/phylogeny_similarity.tsv \
  --output-patterns patterns_binary_PA.txt \
  > pyseer_results_binary_PA.txt


### Pyseer code to run the presence absence data using the continuous anthrone values where each phenotypic value is the Glucose/OD600

pyseer --lmm --phenotypes Data_input/Glucose_phenotype_pyseer.tsv \
  --pres Data_input/gene_presence_absence_rtab_pyseer.tsv \
  --similarity Data_input/phylogeny_similarity.tsv \
  --output-patterns patterns_Glucose_PA.txt \
  > pyseer_results_Glucose_PA.txt


### I will run pyseer now using the vcf files. 

I am using the file strain_118_variants.vcf, and this file shows raw, unfiltered calls. Therefore I start with a filtering step quality > 20, MAF ≥ 0.05, missingness ≤ 20%
                                                                                                                                 
vcftools --vcf strain_118_variants.vcf \
  --minQ 20 --maf 0.05 --max-missing 0.8 \
  --recode --out strain_118_filtered



In the binary phenotype

pyseer --lmm --phenotypes Data_input/Binary_phenotype_pyseer.tsv\
  --vcf Data_input/strain_118_filtered.recode.vcf.gz \
  --similarity Data_input/phylogeny_similarity.tsv \
  --output-patterns patterns_snps_binary.txt \
  > pyseer_snp_results_binary.txt

In the glucose phenotype

pyseer --lmm --phenotypes Data_input/Glucose_phenotype_pyseer.tsv \
  --vcf Data_input/strain_118_filtered.recode.vcf.gz \
  --similarity Data_input/phylogeny_similarity.tsv \
  --output-patterns patterns_snps_glucose.txt \
  > pyseer_snp_results_glucose.txt

# I want to split the multiallelic variatns in two rows so they are not lost. 

# To split those variants I used the following code: 

bcftools norm -m -any strain_118_filtered.recode.vcf.gz -O z -o strain_118_split.vcf.gz
tabix -p vcf strain_118_split.vcf.gz

Then I run both depending on the type of data I was using

In the binary phenotype 

pyseer --lmm --phenotypes Data_input/Binary_phenotype_pyseer.tsv\
  --vcf Data_input/strain_118_split.vcf.gz \
  --similarity Data_input/phylogeny_similarity.tsv \

In the glucose phenotype

  --vcf Data_input/strain_118_split.vcf.gz \
  --similarity Data_input/phylogeny_similarity.tsv \
  --output-patterns patterns_snps_split_glucose.txt \
  > pyseer_snp_results_split_glucose.txt


To calculate the number of genes/SNP variants that covary across all of the strains I used the count_patterns.py that is part of the pyseer github folder. 


Pyseer will test all the SNPs/genes, and it will simultaneously create pattern.txt files that evaluate how many distinct patterns actually exist among all the variants tested. For every tested variant, pyseer writes one line encoding that variant's presence/absence (or genotype) vector across all the strains. Two variants get written as the identical line if they have the exact same 0/1 pattern across every single strain, - same strains carrying it, same strains lacking it, no exception.
```

```{r}
  "qstart","qend","sstart","send","evalue","bitscore"
))

#View(hits)

best_hits <- hits %>%
  group_by(qseqid) %>%
  slice_max(bitscore, n = 1) %>%
  ungroup()

best_hits

## The sseqid matches the "Gene" name in Kayla's document

PrescenceAbsence_original <- read.csv("~/OneDrive - The Pennsylvania State University/Burghardt Lab Shared Folder/Projects/NIFA-AVT-AlfalfaProjects/Aim1bAVT_StrainCollection/Chapter1_Partners_Mariale/Analysis/Genome_EPS/gene_presence_absence.Rtab", sep = "", header = TRUE)

PrescenceAbsence_original

PrescenceAbsence_original

PrescenceAbsence_original


### Merge files 


best_hits_subset <- best_hits %>% select(c("qseqid", "sseqid"))
best_hits_subset
present_or_not <- merge(best_hits_subset, PrescenceAbsence_original, by = "sseqid")
present_or_not

#View(present_or_not)

pa <- present_or_not   
pa <- pa %>% select(-c("EXC", "NIG"))
pa


#View(pa)
strain_cols <- names(pa)[3:ncol(pa)]
strain_cols
pa
gene_variance <- pa %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(n_present = sum(c_across(all_of(strain_cols))),
         n_total   = length(strain_cols)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(qseqid, n_present, n_total)

gene_variance

genes <- gene_variance %>% filter(n_present > 0 & n_present < n_total)   # only the genes worth testing
#View(genes)
genes

Strains

morphotype_df <- tibble(strain = strain_cols) %>%
  mutate(
    strain_num = as.numeric(str_extract(strain, "\\d+")),
    morphotype = if_else(strain_num <= 96, "Mucoid", "Dry")
  )
#morphotype_df

Strains <- Strains %>% select(c("Strain", "Morphology"))
pa
pa_long <- pa %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = all_of(strain_cols), names_to = "Strain", values_to = "present") %>%
  left_join(Strains, by = "Strain") %>%
  group_by(qseqid) %>%
  filter(n_distinct(present) > 1) %>%          # automatically drops invariant genes
  summarise(p_value = fisher.test(table(present, Morphology))$p.value, .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(p_adj = p.adjust(p_value, method = "BH"))   # multiple-testing correction
```

Assessing the phylogenetic signal

```{r}
install.packages("caper")
library(caper)

## Convert dry and mucoid in 0/1

meta_tree <- meta_tree %>%
  mutate(Dry_binary = if_else(Morphology == "Dry", 1, 0))

comp_data <- comparative.data(phy = tree,
                                data = meta_tree,
                                names.col = "Strain_Code",
                                vcv = TRUE)

d_result <- phylo.d(comp_data, binvar = Dry_binary)  # Dry_binary should be 0/1
print(d_result)
plot(d_result)


```
